concepts.name: Algorithm
concepts.definition: An algorithm is a finite, ordered procedure for solving a problem or performing a computation. Important properties are clear steps, defined input and output, termination, and effectiveness.
examples: A sorting algorithm arranges items in order.

concepts.name: Data Structures
concepts.definition: Data structures organize and store data for use by algorithms. Common examples are arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, hash tables, trees, and graphs.
examples: A stack stores items so the last one added is the first one removed.

concepts.name: Array
concepts.definition: An array is an indexed collection of elements.
examples: An array holds items at numeric indexes such as 0, 1, 2.

concepts.name: Linked List
concepts.definition: A linked list is a data structure of nodes connected through references.
examples: Each node points to the next node in the list.

concepts.name: Stack
concepts.definition: A stack is a data structure that is LIFO — Last In, First Out.
examples: The most recently added item is the first one removed.

concepts.name: Queue
concepts.definition: A queue is a data structure that is FIFO — First In, First Out.
examples: The item that has waited longest is served first.

concepts.name: Hash Table
concepts.definition: A hash table stores key-value associations using hashing.
examples: A hash table maps a name to a phone number.

concepts.name: Tree
concepts.definition: A tree is a hierarchical data structure.
examples: A file system is arranged like a tree of folders.

concepts.name: Graph
concepts.definition: G=(V,E) conceptual representation of vertices and edges.
examples: A network map can be modelled as vertices joined by edges.

concepts.name: Algorithmic Complexity
concepts.definition: Algorithmic complexity describes how an algorithm's cost grows with input size. Big-O describes asymptotic growth rather than exact runtime.
examples: O(n log n) grows faster than O(n) but slower than O(n squared).
misconceptions: Big-O does not measure exact runtime in seconds.
concepts.formula: O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n^2), O(2^n), O(n!)

concepts.name: Variable
concepts.definition: A variable is a named element of a program that holds data used in expressions and statements.
examples: A variable stores a number that a loop counts with.

concepts.name: Constant
concepts.definition: A constant is a program element whose value is fixed rather than changing during execution.
examples: A constant holds a value such as a maximum limit.

concepts.name: Data Type
concepts.definition: A data type classifies what kind of data a value holds and how a program may use it.
examples: Numbers and text are different data types.

concepts.name: Expression
concepts.definition: An expression is a combination of values and operators that evaluates to a result.
examples: Adding two variables produces an expression.

concepts.name: Statement
concepts.definition: A statement is a single instruction in a program that is executed in order.
examples: Assigning a value to a variable is a statement.

concepts.name: Function
concepts.definition: A function is a named block of code that performs a task and can be reused, accepting parameters and possibly returning a result.
examples: A function calculates the total of a list of numbers.

concepts.name: Parameter
concepts.definition: A parameter is the named input listed in a function definition that the function expects when it is called.
examples: A function that adds two numbers declares two parameters.

concepts.name: Argument
concepts.definition: An argument is the value actually passed to a function when the function is called.
examples: Calling add with 2 and 3 passes two arguments.

concepts.name: Loop
concepts.definition: A loop repeats a block of code while a condition holds or for each item in a sequence.
examples: A loop walks through every element of an array.

concepts.name: Condition
concepts.definition: A condition is a statement that tests whether something is true so the program can choose a path.
examples: A condition checks whether a value exceeds a limit.

concepts.name: Object
concepts.definition: An object is an instance that combines data and behavior, created from a class.
examples: A user record object holds fields and actions.

concepts.name: Class
concepts.definition: A class defines the data and behavior that its objects will have.
examples: A class describes the fields shared by many objects.

concepts.name: Module
concepts.definition: A module is a unit of code that can be grouped and reused by other parts of a program.
examples: A module groups related functions in one file.

concepts.name: Exception
concepts.definition: An exception is an error condition raised while a program runs, which can be handled instead of crashing the program.
examples: A program catches an exception when input is invalid.

concepts.name: Object-Oriented Programming
concepts.definition: Object-oriented programming is a style of building programs from objects. Its core concepts commonly taught are encapsulation, abstraction, inheritance, and polymorphism.
examples: A program models entities as classes with state and behavior.

concepts.name: Encapsulation
concepts.definition: Encapsulation is a core object-oriented concept of bundling data together with the operations that use it.
examples: An object keeps its internal data with its own methods.

concepts.name: Abstraction
concepts.definition: Abstraction is a core object-oriented concept of exposing what a component does while hiding how it works.
examples: A user works with a simple interface while details stay hidden.

concepts.name: Inheritance
concepts.definition: Inheritance is a core object-oriented concept in which one class builds on another.
examples: A specialized class reuses the structure of a general class.

concepts.name: Polymorphism
concepts.definition: Polymorphism is a core object-oriented concept that lets different kinds of objects be used through the same expectation.
examples: Different objects respond in their own way to the same action.

concepts.name: Database
concepts.definition: A database is a structured collection of data. Key concepts are table, row, column, primary key, foreign key, index, query, transaction, and normalization.
examples: A database stores records in tables that queries can retrieve.

concepts.name: Table
concepts.definition: A table is a structured part of a database made of rows and columns.
examples: A customers table stores one row per customer.

concepts.name: Row
concepts.definition: A row is a single record in a database table; a primary key uniquely identifies a row.
examples: Each row in a students table is one student.

concepts.name: Column
concepts.definition: A column is one of the key database elements of a table, holding the same kind of value for every row.
examples: A column named age stores an age for every row.

concepts.name: Primary Key
concepts.definition: A primary key uniquely identifies a row in a table.
examples: An order id column can serve as the primary key of an orders table.

concepts.name: Foreign Key
concepts.definition: A foreign key references a key in another table.
examples: An orders table references the customer id in a customers table.

concepts.name: Index
concepts.definition: An index is a data structure that can accelerate queries at the cost of storage and write or update overhead.
examples: Indexing an email column speeds lookups by email.
misconceptions: An index speeds reads but adds cost to writes and updates.

concepts.name: Query
concepts.definition: A query requests data from a database, commonly written in SQL with clauses such as WHERE, ORDER BY, GROUP BY, HAVING, JOIN, and LIMIT.
examples: A query returns rows that match a condition.

concepts.name: Transaction
concepts.definition: A transaction is a logical unit of database work. Transactions are described by the ACID properties: atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability.
examples: Moving money between accounts is done as one transaction.

concepts.name: Normalization
concepts.definition: Normalization is a database design practice applied to tables and relationships as part of structuring data.
examples: Related data is split into separate linked tables.

concepts.name: SQL
concepts.definition: SQL is the language used to work with database data. Common commands are SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, ALTER, and DROP, with clauses such as WHERE, ORDER BY, GROUP BY, HAVING, JOIN, and LIMIT.
examples: A SELECT statement retrieves rows matching a WHERE clause.

concepts.name: Networking
concepts.definition: Networking covers how devices connect and communicate. Core concepts include IP address, MAC address, DNS, HTTP, HTTPS, TCP, UDP, router, switch, port, and packet.
examples: Devices exchange packets through routers and switches.

concepts.name: IP Address
concepts.definition: IP is the network-layer protocol used for addressing and routing packets, and an IP address identifies a device on a network.
examples: A router uses IP addresses to forward packets to the right destination.

concepts.name: MAC Address
concepts.definition: A MAC address identifies a device on a local network, and switches forward frames using MAC addresses.
examples: A switch looks at MAC addresses to deliver a frame.

concepts.name: DNS
concepts.definition: DNS maps domain names to network addresses and related records. Common record types are A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, and TXT.
examples: DNS turns a domain name into an address a network can route to.
concepts.formula: A -> IPv4, AAAA -> IPv6, CNAME -> canonical name, MX -> mail exchange, TXT -> text metadata

concepts.name: HTTP
concepts.definition: HTTP is the protocol used to transfer web data. A request carries a method, URL, headers, and an optional body, and a response carries a status, headers, and an optional body.
examples: A browser sends a GET request and receives a response body.

concepts.name: HTTPS
concepts.definition: HTTPS normally uses HTTP over TLS, the cryptographic protocol used to secure network communications.
examples: A site served over HTTPS protects traffic between browser and server.

concepts.name: TCP
concepts.definition: TCP is connection-oriented transport with reliability mechanisms.
examples: Web traffic commonly travels over TCP to guarantee delivery.

concepts.name: UDP
concepts.definition: UDP is connectionless transport with lower overhead and no built-in guarantee of delivery.
examples: Streaming or lookups may use UDP when speed matters more than guarantees.

concepts.name: Router
concepts.definition: A router forwards traffic between networks.
examples: A router passes packets between a local network and the internet.

concepts.name: Switch
concepts.definition: A switch connects devices within a local network and forwards frames using MAC addresses.
examples: A switch delivers a frame only to the port of its destination device.

concepts.name: Functional Requirement
concepts.definition: A functional requirement describes what a system should do.

concepts.name: Non-functional Requirement
concepts.definition: A non-functional requirement describes qualities or constraints such as performance, reliability, security, and usability.

concepts.name: Layered Architecture
concepts.definition: A common architectural idea orders layers as Presentation, then Application / Domain, then Data.

concepts.name: MVC
concepts.definition: MVC is one of the common software architecture patterns listed alongside MVVM, Clean Architecture, the Repository pattern, and Dependency Injection.

concepts.name: MVVM
concepts.definition: MVVM is one of the common software architecture patterns listed alongside MVC, Clean Architecture, the Repository pattern, and Dependency Injection.

concepts.name: Clean Architecture
concepts.definition: Clean Architecture is one of the common software architecture patterns listed with MVC, MVVM, the Repository pattern, and Dependency Injection.

concepts.name: Repository Pattern
concepts.definition: The Repository pattern abstracts data access behind a repository interface and is listed among common architecture patterns.

concepts.name: Dependency Injection
concepts.definition: Dependency injection supplies dependencies from outside a class or module instead of constructing all dependencies internally, and is listed among common architecture patterns.

concepts.name: Unit Testing
concepts.definition: Unit testing is one of the common types of testing, listed alongside integration, system, regression, UI, and acceptance testing. It verifies individual units of the software.

concepts.name: Integration Testing
concepts.definition: Integration testing is one of the common types of testing; it checks that combined components work together.

concepts.name: System Testing
concepts.definition: System testing is one of the common types of testing; it evaluates the system as a whole.

concepts.name: Regression Testing
concepts.definition: Regression testing is one of the common types of testing; it rechecks existing behavior after changes, and it is also a step in the recommended debugging workflow.

concepts.name: UI Testing
concepts.definition: UI testing is one of the common types of testing; it exercises the user interface.

concepts.name: Acceptance Testing
concepts.definition: Acceptance testing is one of the common types of testing; it checks whether the system is acceptable against requirements.

concepts.name: Debugging
concepts.definition: The recommended debugging workflow is: reproduce, isolate, inspect logs, identify root cause, make minimal fix, test, and regression test.
examples: Reproduce → isolate → inspect logs → identify root cause → make minimal fix → test → regression test

concepts.name: HTML
concepts.definition: HTML is the standard markup language for creating the structure of web pages. Common HTML elements include html, head, body, header, nav, main, section, article, footer, headings, p, a, img, button, form, input, textarea, select, and table.

concepts.name: Head
concepts.definition: The head element is a common HTML element for the document head.

concepts.name: Body
concepts.definition: The body element is a common HTML element that contains the visible content of the page.

concepts.name: Header
concepts.definition: The header element is a common HTML element for header content.

concepts.name: Nav
concepts.definition: The nav element is a common HTML element for navigation sections.

concepts.name: Main
concepts.definition: The main element is a common HTML element for the main content of the document.

concepts.name: Section
concepts.definition: The section element is a common HTML element for a thematic section of content.

concepts.name: Article
concepts.definition: The article element is a common HTML element for self-contained article content.

concepts.name: Footer
concepts.definition: The footer element is a common HTML element for footer content.

concepts.name: Heading
concepts.definition: Headings are the common HTML elements h1 through h6, used to structure document titles.

concepts.name: Paragraph
concepts.definition: The p element is a common HTML element for a paragraph of text.

concepts.name: Anchor
concepts.definition: The a element is a common HTML element for links between pages and locations.

concepts.name: Image
concepts.definition: The img element is a common HTML element for embedding images.

concepts.name: Button
concepts.definition: The button element is a common HTML element for clickable buttons in a page or form.

concepts.name: Form
concepts.definition: The form element is a common HTML element for collecting user input.

concepts.name: Input
concepts.definition: The input element is a common HTML element for a single form input field.

concepts.name: Textarea
concepts.definition: The textarea element is a common HTML element for multi-line text input.

concepts.name: Select
concepts.definition: The select element is a common HTML element for choosing one option from a list.

concepts.name: HTML Table
concepts.definition: The table element is a common HTML element for displaying tabular data in a page.

concepts.name: Cascade
concepts.definition: The cascade is one of the core CSS concepts, together with specificity, inheritance, the box model, Flexbox, Grid, positioning, media queries, transitions, and animations.

concepts.name: Specificity
concepts.definition: Specificity is one of the core CSS concepts that determines which competing style rules apply.

concepts.name: CSS Inheritance
concepts.definition: Inheritance is one of the core CSS concepts describing how styles pass from parent elements to their children.

concepts.name: Box Model
concepts.definition: The CSS box model layers content, then padding, then border, then margin.

concepts.name: Flexbox
concepts.definition: Flexbox is one of the core CSS layout concepts for arranging items along a flex axis.

concepts.name: Grid
concepts.definition: Grid is one of the core CSS layout concepts for two-dimensional page layout.

concepts.name: Positioning
concepts.definition: Positioning is one of the core CSS concepts for placing elements in the page.

concepts.name: Media Queries
concepts.definition: Media queries are one of the core CSS concepts used to make styles adapt to different screen sizes and conditions.

concepts.name: Transitions
concepts.definition: Transitions are one of the core CSS concepts for animating changes between style states.

concepts.name: Animations
concepts.definition: Animations are one of the core CSS concepts for continuous style motion.

concepts.name: Android
concepts.definition: Android development knowledge covers components such as Activity, Service, Broadcast receiver, Content provider, Intent, and Manifest, plus modern technologies such as Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Android SDK, Gradle, ViewModel, StateFlow, Room, WorkManager, and Navigation.

concepts.name: Activity
concepts.definition: An Activity is the UI entry point or component for a user interaction flow in Android.

concepts.name: Service
concepts.definition: A Service is an Android component for longer-running operations, with restrictions defined by modern Android background execution rules.

concepts.name: Broadcast Receiver
concepts.definition: A broadcast receiver is an Android component that responds to broadcast messages and events.

concepts.name: Content Provider
concepts.definition: A content provider is one of the common Android components used to manage access to structured data.

concepts.name: Intent
concepts.definition: An intent is a message object used to request actions or communicate between Android components.

concepts.name: Application
concepts.definition: The application is one of the common Android components; the manifest declares components, permissions, and application metadata.

concepts.name: Manifest
concepts.definition: The manifest declares Android components, permissions, and application metadata.

concepts.name: Permissions
concepts.definition: Android permissions are sensitive capabilities that should be requested only when required.

concepts.name: Kotlin
concepts.definition: Kotlin is listed among the common modern Android technologies, used alongside Jetpack Compose, Android SDK, Gradle, ViewModel, and Room.

concepts.name: Jetpack Compose
concepts.definition: Jetpack Compose is a declarative UI framework for Android.

concepts.name: Android SDK
concepts.definition: The Android SDK is listed among the common modern Android technologies for building Android applications.

concepts.name: Gradle
concepts.definition: Gradle resolves dependencies and builds application variants in an Android project.

concepts.name: Android Build
concepts.definition: The Android build uses Gradle to resolve dependencies and build application variants. Common build types are debug and release.

concepts.name: Build Types
concepts.definition: Common Android build types include debug and release.

concepts.name: Product Flavors
concepts.definition: Product flavors allow build variants for different configurations or products.

concepts.name: Signing
concepts.definition: Release Android applications require an appropriate signing configuration.

concepts.name: Android Project Structure
concepts.definition: Common areas of an Android project are the app module, manifests, source sets, resources, Gradle configuration, and tests.

concepts.name: ViewModel
concepts.definition: A ViewModel stores UI-related state and logic across configuration changes within its scope.

concepts.name: Room
concepts.definition: Room is a persistence abstraction over SQLite for Android.

concepts.name: Room Components
concepts.definition: Room components include Entity, DAO, and Database.

concepts.name: WorkManager
concepts.definition: WorkManager is used for deferrable persistent background work on Android.

concepts.name: Navigation
concepts.definition: Navigation is listed among the common modern Android technologies for moving between screens in an app.

concepts.name: Composable
concepts.definition: A composable is a function that describes UI from the current state.

concepts.name: State
concepts.definition: Android state-driven UI flow: State → UI → user event → ViewModel or action → new state → UI recomposes.
examples: State → UI → user event → ViewModel/action → new state → UI recomposes

concepts.name: Recomposition
concepts.definition: Recomposition is when Compose reruns affected composables when observed state changes.

concepts.name: Modifier
concepts.definition: Modifier is a core Compose concept used to decorate composables with styling and behavior.

concepts.name: Compose Column
concepts.definition: Column is a core Compose layout component listed among Compose concepts.

concepts.name: Compose Row
concepts.definition: Row is a core Compose layout component listed among Compose concepts.

concepts.name: Box
concepts.definition: Box is a core Compose layout component listed among Compose concepts.

concepts.name: LazyColumn
concepts.definition: LazyColumn is a core Compose concept listed among Compose concepts for building scrolling lists.

concepts.name: Scaffold
concepts.definition: Scaffold is a core Compose concept listed among Compose concepts for structuring screens.

concepts.name: MaterialTheme
concepts.definition: MaterialTheme is a core Compose concept for applying Material styling to a Compose UI.

concepts.name: State Hoisting
concepts.definition: State hoisting means moving state to the lowest common ancestor that needs to coordinate it.

concepts.name: Kotlin Coroutines
concepts.definition: Kotlin coroutines are a structured concurrency mechanism for asynchronous work.

concepts.name: Flow
concepts.definition: A flow is an asynchronous stream of values.

concepts.name: StateFlow
concepts.definition: StateFlow is a state-holder observable stream.

concepts.name: SharedFlow
concepts.definition: A shared flow is a hot stream useful for events and shared emissions.

concepts.name: Python
concepts.definition: Python knowledge covers variables, strings, lists, tuples, sets, dictionaries, conditions, loops, functions, classes, exceptions, modules, packages, files, JSON, HTTP APIs, asyncio, testing, and virtual environments.

concepts.name: List
concepts.definition: A list is a core Python collection topic; example concepts create a list of numbers and sum it.

concepts.name: Tuple
concepts.definition: A tuple is one of the core Python collection topics listed alongside lists, sets, and dictionaries.

concepts.name: Set
concepts.definition: A set is one of the core Python collection topics listed alongside lists, tuples, and dictionaries.

concepts.name: Dictionary
concepts.definition: A dictionary is one of the core Python collection topics, used for key-value data.

concepts.name: asyncio
concepts.definition: asyncio is a Python core topic for writing asynchronous code alongside HTTP APIs, testing, and virtual environments.

concepts.name: Virtual Environment
concepts.definition: A virtual environment is a Python core topic for creating an isolated environment for a project's dependencies.

concepts.name: JavaScript
concepts.definition: JavaScript core concepts include let, const, function, arrow function, object, array, map, filter, reduce, promise, async/await, DOM, event, module, JSON, and fetch.
examples: async function loadData() { const response = await fetch(url); return await response.json(); }

concepts.name: let and const
concepts.definition: let and const are declarations listed among JavaScript's core concepts for variables and constants.

concepts.name: Arrow Function
concepts.definition: The arrow function is a JavaScript function form listed among the language's core concepts.

concepts.name: Map
concepts.definition: map is listed among JavaScript's core concepts for transforming the elements of a collection into a new collection.

concepts.name: Filter
concepts.definition: filter is listed among JavaScript's core concepts for selecting elements that match a condition.

concepts.name: Reduce
concepts.definition: reduce is listed among JavaScript's core concepts for accumulating a collection into a single result.

concepts.name: Promise
concepts.definition: A promise or future represents a result that may become available later, and it is listed among JavaScript's core concepts.

concepts.name: Async/Await
concepts.definition: Asynchronous programming allows operations to progress without blocking the entire execution flow while waiting for I/O or other tasks. async/await is the modern JavaScript pattern for it.
examples: async function loadData() { const response = await fetch(url); return await response.json(); }

concepts.name: DOM
concepts.definition: DOM is listed among JavaScript's core concepts for representing and interacting with the page structure.

concepts.name: Event
concepts.definition: Events are listed among JavaScript's core concepts for responding to actions in the browser.

concepts.name: Fetch
concepts.definition: fetch is listed among JavaScript's core concepts and is used to request data, commonly with async/await.

concepts.name: Artificial Intelligence
concepts.definition: Artificial intelligence is the broad field of building systems capable of performing tasks associated with abilities such as perception, reasoning, learning, language processing, and decision-making.

concepts.name: Machine Learning
concepts.definition: Machine learning uses algorithms that learn patterns from data. Common categories are supervised learning, unsupervised learning, and reinforcement learning.

concepts.name: Supervised Learning
concepts.definition: Supervised learning learns from labeled examples and is one of the common machine learning categories.

concepts.name: Unsupervised Learning
concepts.definition: Unsupervised learning finds structure in data without explicit target labels and is one of the common machine learning categories.

concepts.name: Reinforcement Learning
concepts.definition: In reinforcement learning, an agent learns from interaction using rewards and penalties, and it is one of the common machine learning categories.

concepts.name: Neural Network
concepts.definition: Common neural network components are the input layer, hidden layers, output layer, weights, biases, and activation functions.

concepts.name: Deep Learning
concepts.definition: Deep learning is listed among the core AI terms alongside artificial intelligence, machine learning, neural networks, and generative AI.

concepts.name: Generative AI
concepts.definition: Generative models can produce content such as text, images, audio, video, and code.

concepts.name: Large Language Model
concepts.definition: A large language model is listed among the core AI terms and works with concepts such as tokens, context windows, prompts, and inference.

concepts.name: Computer Vision
concepts.definition: Computer vision is listed among the core AI terms for perception-related abilities of AI systems.

concepts.name: Speech Recognition
concepts.definition: Speech recognition is listed among the core AI terms for converting spoken language into text.

concepts.name: Natural Language Processing
concepts.definition: Natural language processing is listed among the core AI terms and is associated with language-processing abilities such as those used by large language models.

concepts.name: Token
concepts.definition: A token is an important large language model term for the units of text a model processes.

concepts.name: Context Window
concepts.definition: The context window is an important large language model term for the content available to the model during generation.

concepts.name: Prompt
concepts.definition: A prompt is an important large language model term for the input given to a model, often paired with a system instruction.

concepts.name: System Instruction
concepts.definition: A system instruction is an important large language model term for instruction content supplied to the model.

concepts.name: Temperature
concepts.definition: Temperature is an important large language model term that influences how varied the model's outputs are.

concepts.name: Embedding
concepts.definition: An embedding is a vector representation of data such as text.

concepts.name: Retrieval
concepts.definition: Retrieval is the step that gathers relevant context for a query before model generation in a retrieval-augmented flow.
examples: User query → retrieval → relevant context → model generation → grounded response

concepts.name: RAG
concepts.definition: Retrieval-Augmented Generation combines retrieval with generation to ground answers in supplied knowledge. It commonly follows: user query → retrieval → relevant context → model generation → grounded response.
examples: User query → retrieval → relevant context → model generation → grounded response

concepts.name: Fine-tuning
concepts.definition: Fine-tuning is an important large language model term for adapting a trained model further.

concepts.name: Inference
concepts.definition: Inference is using a trained model to produce outputs.

concepts.name: Hallucination
concepts.definition: A hallucination is generated content that is unsupported or factually incorrect.

concepts.name: JSON
concepts.definition: JSON is structured key-value data. It is a common data format and also a Python and JavaScript core topic.

concepts.name: CSV
concepts.definition: CSV is tabular comma-separated data.

concepts.name: XML
concepts.definition: XML is markup-based structured data.

concepts.name: Markdown
concepts.definition: Markdown is lightweight text formatting syntax.

concepts.name: PDF
concepts.definition: PDF is a portable document format.

concepts.name: TXT
concepts.definition: TXT is plain text.

concepts.name: ZIP
concepts.definition: ZIP is an archive container commonly used to bundle files.

concepts.name: Internet
concepts.definition: The Internet is a global network of interconnected networks using standardized communication protocols.

concepts.name: Browser
concepts.definition: A browser is software used to access and interact with web content.

concepts.name: Search Engine
concepts.definition: A search engine is a system that indexes and retrieves information from available sources.

concepts.name: Cloud Computing
concepts.definition: Cloud computing is computing resources delivered through networked services rather than being limited to a user's local machine.

concepts.name: Cybersecurity
concepts.definition: Cybersecurity fundamentals cover the CIA triad, authentication, authorization, encryption, hashing, threats, vulnerabilities, risk, exploits, least privilege, defense in depth, secure password storage, MFA, phishing, social engineering, and backups.

concepts.name: CIA Triad
concepts.definition: The CIA triad consists of confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

concepts.name: Authentication
concepts.definition: Authentication verifies who a user or system is.
misconceptions: Authentication and authorization are the same thing. Authentication verifies who you are; authorization determines what you are allowed to do.

concepts.name: Authorization
aliases: what are you allowed to do
concepts.definition: Authorization determines what an authenticated user or system is permitted to do.

concepts.name: Encryption
concepts.definition: Encryption transforms information using a cryptographic process so that only authorized parties with the necessary key can recover the intended plaintext.
misconceptions: Encryption is one-way like hashing. Encryption is reversible with the key, while hashing is designed to be one-way.

concepts.name: Hashing
concepts.definition: Hashing is a one-way transformation used for purposes such as integrity checks and password storage designs.
misconceptions: Hashing can be reversed like encryption. Hashing is designed to be one-way, while encryption is reversible with the key.

concepts.name: Threat
concepts.definition: A threat is a potential cause of harm.

concepts.name: Vulnerability
concepts.definition: A vulnerability is a weakness that can be exploited.

concepts.name: Risk
concepts.definition: Risk is the combination of likelihood and impact in a defined risk model.

concepts.name: Exploit
concepts.definition: An exploit is a technique or code used to take advantage of a vulnerability.

concepts.name: Least Privilege
concepts.definition: Least privilege means giving each identity or process only the access required.

concepts.name: Defense in Depth
concepts.definition: Defense in depth uses multiple layers of protection.

concepts.name: Secure Password Storage
concepts.definition: Secure password storage uses a password-hashing scheme designed for passwords, with salts and appropriate work factors; plaintext passwords should not be stored.

concepts.name: MFA
concepts.definition: Multi-factor authentication combines different factor categories.

concepts.name: Phishing
concepts.definition: Phishing is a fraudulent attempt to obtain information or induce unsafe actions through deceptive communications.

concepts.name: Social Engineering
concepts.definition: Social engineering manipulates people rather than only exploiting technical systems.

concepts.name: Backup
concepts.definition: A backup maintains recoverable copies of important data.

concepts.name: 3-2-1 Backup Principle
concepts.definition: The 3-2-1 backup principle is a common backup strategy: 3 copies, 2 different media, 1 off-site copy.

concepts.name: One-to-One
concepts.definition: In a one-to-one relationship, one record corresponds to at most one record in another relation.

concepts.name: One-to-Many
concepts.definition: In a one-to-many relationship, one record can relate to many records.

concepts.name: Many-to-Many
concepts.definition: In a many-to-many relationship, many records on one side can relate to many on the other, normally implemented using a junction table.

concepts.name: Frontend
concepts.definition: The frontend runs primarily in the user's browser and handles presentation and interaction.

concepts.name: Backend
concepts.definition: The backend provides server-side processing, data access, authentication, business logic, APIs, and other services.

concepts.name: API
concepts.definition: An API is a defined interface through which software components communicate.

concepts.name: REST
concepts.definition: REST is an architectural style commonly used for networked APIs.

concepts.name: JSON API
concepts.definition: A JSON API is a common way of representing structured request and response data.

concepts.name: Software Architecture
concepts.definition: A recommended conceptual flow is UI → Chat Controller → Conversation Context → Intent Classifier → Request Planner (local knowledge, code assistant, attachment, other provider) → Response → Persistence. The UI should not contain knowledge logic, the database should not contain provider-routing logic, and each layer should have one clear responsibility.
examples: UI → Chat Controller → Conversation Context → Intent Classifier → Request Planner → Response → Persistence

concepts.name: Computer System
concepts.definition: A computer system consists of hardware plus software plus data plus users and procedures.

concepts.name: CPU
concepts.definition: A CPU includes a control unit, an arithmetic/logic unit, registers, and cache.

concepts.name: RAM
concepts.definition: RAM is volatile working memory.

concepts.name: ROM
concepts.definition: ROM is non-volatile memory traditionally used for firmware or fixed instructions, though modern systems use various flash-based implementations.

concepts.name: Storage
concepts.definition: Common storage forms include HDD, SSD, flash storage, and optical media.

concepts.name: Operating System
concepts.definition: An operating system manages hardware and provides services for applications. Its responsibilities include process, memory, file, and device management, security, and the user interface.

concepts.name: Process
concepts.definition: A process is a program in execution.

concepts.name: Thread
concepts.definition: A thread is a unit of execution within a process.

concepts.name: Concurrency
concepts.definition: Concurrency means multiple tasks make progress during overlapping periods.
misconceptions: Concurrency and parallelism are the same. Concurrency is tasks making progress during overlapping periods; parallelism is computations executing simultaneously on multiple processing resources.

concepts.name: Parallelism
concepts.definition: Parallelism means multiple computations execute simultaneously on multiple processing resources.

concepts.name: Deadlock
concepts.definition: A deadlock occurs when a set of processes becomes permanently blocked because each is waiting for resources or events held by others.

concepts.name: Relational Database
concepts.definition: A relational database organizes data into related tables.

concepts.name: ACID
concepts.definition: ACID stands for atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability — the properties of reliable database transactions.

concepts.name: NoSQL
concepts.definition: NoSQL is a broad family of non-relational database systems, including document, key-value, wide-column, and graph databases.

concepts.name: Cache
concepts.definition: Fast memory reducing the average time needed to access frequently used data. Cache levels are often L1, L2 and L3 with different size and speed characteristics.

concepts.name: CDN
concepts.definition: A CDN is a distributed network that delivers cached content closer to users.

concepts.name: TLS
concepts.definition: TLS is a cryptographic protocol used to secure network communications; HTTPS normally uses HTTP over TLS.

concepts.name: Port
concepts.definition: A port is a logical endpoint number associated with network services. Common ports are HTTP → 80, HTTPS → 443, SSH → 22, and DNS → 53.

concepts.name: DNS Records
concepts.definition: DNS records map domain names to network addresses and related records: A → IPv4 address, AAAA → IPv6 address, CNAME → canonical name, MX → mail exchange, TXT → text metadata.

concepts.name: Software License
concepts.definition: A license determines conditions for using, modifying, and distributing software. Permissive open-source examples are MIT, BSD, and Apache 2.0, and a copyleft example is GPL; always inspect the actual license.

concepts.name: Version Control
concepts.definition: Version control records changes using commits, branches, merges, rebases, and merge conflicts.

concepts.name: Commit
concepts.definition: A commit is a snapshot-like recorded change in version control.

concepts.name: Branch
concepts.definition: A branch is an independent line of development in version control.

concepts.name: Merge
concepts.definition: A merge combines histories in version control.

concepts.name: Rebase
concepts.definition: Replays commits onto a new base; changes commit history.

concepts.name: Merge Conflict
concepts.definition: A merge conflict occurs when Git cannot automatically determine how to combine competing changes.

concepts.name: CI/CD
concepts.definition: Continuous integration and continuous delivery/deployment automate parts of building, testing, and releasing software.

concepts.name: Environment Variables
concepts.definition: Environment variables are configuration values supplied outside source code; secrets should not be hardcoded into repositories.

concepts.name: Secret Management
concepts.definition: API keys, passwords, tokens, and private credentials should be stored using appropriate secret-management mechanisms.

concepts.name: Programming Paradigm
concepts.definition: Common programming paradigms are imperative, declarative, functional, object-oriented, event-driven, and concurrent.

concepts.name: Recursion
concepts.definition: A function calls itself with a smaller or subproblem input and requires a base case.

concepts.name: Syntax Error
concepts.definition: A syntax error occurs when program structure violates language grammar.

concepts.name: Runtime Error
concepts.definition: A runtime error is a failure during execution.

concepts.name: Logic Error
concepts.definition: A logic error occurs when the program runs but produces incorrect behavior.

concepts.name: Static Typing
concepts.definition: With static typing, types are checked substantially before runtime.

concepts.name: Dynamic Typing
concepts.definition: With dynamic typing, types are associated with runtime values and checked during execution.

concepts.name: Null/Optional
concepts.definition: Null or optional values represent the absence of a value; languages handle this differently.

concepts.name: Immutability
concepts.definition: An immutable value cannot be changed after creation; updates produce new values in systems that use immutable data structures.

concepts.name: Pure Function
concepts.definition: A pure function gives the same output for the same input and has no observable side effects.
examples: Same input → same output and no observable side effects

concepts.name: Higher-order Function
concepts.definition: A higher-order function takes functions as arguments or returns a function.

concepts.name: Closure
concepts.definition: A closure is when a function retains access to variables from its surrounding lexical scope.

concepts.name: HTTP Request
concepts.definition: An HTTP request consists of method, URL, headers, and an optional body.

concepts.name: HTTP Response
concepts.definition: An HTTP response consists of status, headers, and an optional body.

concepts.name: Cookies
concepts.definition: Cookies are small pieces of state associated with web requests.

concepts.name: Local Storage
concepts.definition: Local storage is browser-side persistent key-value storage.

concepts.name: Session Storage
concepts.definition: Session storage is browser-side storage associated with a browsing session.

concepts.name: CORS
concepts.definition: CORS is a browser security mechanism governing cross-origin requests.

concepts.name: Same-Origin
concepts.definition: Under the same-origin concept, an origin is generally defined by scheme, host, and port.

concepts.name: XSS
concepts.definition: Cross-site scripting involves injecting executable content into a context where it can execute in another user's browser.

concepts.name: SQL Injection
concepts.definition: SQL injection occurs when untrusted input changes the intended structure of a database query.

concepts.name: CSRF
concepts.definition: Cross-site request forgery tricks a user's authenticated browser into making an unintended request.

concepts.name: Secure Web Practices
concepts.definition: Secure web practices include validating input, encoding output appropriately, using parameterized database queries, protecting authentication, using HTTPS, applying least privilege, keeping dependencies updated, and avoiding exposing secrets.

concepts.name: Frontend State
concepts.definition: Common frontend state categories are local UI state, form state, server/cache state, and global application state.

concepts.name: Responsive Design
concepts.definition: Responsive design means interfaces adapt to different screen sizes and input methods.

concepts.name: Accessibility
concepts.definition: Important accessibility practices include semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, visible focus, appropriate labels, sufficient contrast, alternative text, and meaningful headings.

concepts.name: Training
concepts.definition: During training, model parameters are adjusted using data and an optimization objective.

concepts.name: Overfitting
concepts.definition: Overfitting is when a model performs very well on training data but poorly on unseen data.

concepts.name: Underfitting
concepts.definition: Underfitting is when a model is too simple to capture important patterns.

concepts.name: Generalization
concepts.definition: Generalization is performance on unseen data.

concepts.name: Train/Validation/Test
concepts.definition: Training data fits the model, validation data tunes choices, and test data provides final evaluation.

concepts.name: Vector Database
concepts.definition: A vector database is optimized for similarity search over vector representations.

concepts.name: Chunking
concepts.definition: Chunking is splitting documents into retrievable pieces.

concepts.name: Reranking
concepts.definition: Reranking reorders retrieved candidates according to relevance.

concepts.name: Grounding
concepts.definition: Grounding constrains or supports model outputs using trusted evidence or context.

concepts.name: Prompt Injection
concepts.definition: Prompt injection is when untrusted content attempts to alter the behavior or instructions of an AI system.

concepts.name: Separation of Concerns
concepts.definition: Separation of concerns keeps UI, state, intent, retrieval, provider routing, persistence, attachment processing, and response rendering separate.

concepts.name: Adapter
concepts.definition: An adapter converts one interface into another expected by a component.

concepts.name: Facade
concepts.definition: A facade provides a simpler interface over a complex subsystem.

concepts.name: Observer
concepts.definition: The observer pattern lets objects subscribe to state or event changes.

concepts.name: Singleton
concepts.definition: A singleton is one shared instance; use it carefully because excessive global state complicates testing and lifecycle management.
misconceptions: Singletons are always harmless. Excessive global state complicates testing and lifecycle management.

concepts.name: DRY
concepts.definition: DRY means avoid unnecessary duplication.

concepts.name: KISS
concepts.definition: KISS means prefer simple solutions when they adequately solve the problem.

concepts.name: YAGNI
concepts.definition: YAGNI means do not implement speculative functionality without a current requirement.

concepts.name: SOLID
concepts.definition: SOLID stands for Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, and Dependency Inversion.

concepts.name: OSI Model
concepts.definition: The OSI model has seven layers: physical, data link, network, transport, session, presentation, and application.

concepts.name: NAT
concepts.definition: NAT translates network addresses between network contexts.

concepts.name: DHCP
concepts.definition: DHCP automatically provides network configuration such as IP address and gateway.

concepts.name: Latency
concepts.definition: Latency is the time delay in a network communication.

concepts.name: Bandwidth
concepts.definition: Bandwidth is the capacity of a communication channel.
misconceptions: Bandwidth and throughput are the same. Bandwidth is the capacity of a channel; throughput is the actual rate of successful data transfer.

concepts.name: Throughput
concepts.definition: Throughput is the actual rate of successful data transfer.

concepts.name: Packet Loss
concepts.definition: Packet loss occurs when packets fail to reach their destination.

concepts.name: Ping
concepts.definition: Ping is a common diagnostic tool using ICMP echo messages.

concepts.name: Instruction Set
concepts.definition: Collection of machine-level operations supported by a processor architecture.

concepts.name: Register
concepts.definition: Small, fast storage location within a processor.

concepts.name: Pipelining
concepts.definition: Overlaps stages of instruction processing.

concepts.name: Branch Prediction
concepts.definition: Processor predicts control-flow decisions to reduce pipeline stalls.

concepts.name: GPU
concepts.definition: Processor optimized for massively parallel workloads such as graphics and certain numerical or AI workloads.

concepts.name: TPU/NPU
concepts.definition: Specialized accelerator classes designed for neural-network or AI operations.

concepts.name: Kernel
concepts.definition: Core operating-system component managing resources and privileged operations.

concepts.name: User Space
concepts.definition: Less-privileged environment where ordinary applications commonly execute.

concepts.name: System Call
concepts.definition: Interface through which applications request operating system services.

concepts.name: Process Scheduling
concepts.definition: Selects processes or threads for CPU execution.

concepts.name: Virtual Memory
concepts.definition: Abstraction allowing processes to use virtual address spaces and enabling memory-management techniques such as paging.
misconceptions: More RAM always means a faster device. Performance depends on workload, CPU, storage, thermals, software and other factors; more RAM helps only when memory is a limiting factor.

concepts.name: Page
concepts.definition: Fixed-size virtual-memory unit in typical paging systems.

concepts.name: Swap
concepts.definition: Disk-backed extension of memory used under some operating system configurations.

concepts.name: File System
concepts.definition: Organizes persistent data into files, directories and metadata.
misconceptions: An SSD is always faster at everything. SSDs are typically much faster than HDDs for storage access, but application performance also depends on CPU, memory, interface and workload.

concepts.name: Permissions
concepts.definition: Controls access by users and processes.

concepts.name: Interrupt
concepts.definition: Signal requesting processor attention from hardware or software events.

concepts.name: Compiler
concepts.definition: Transforms source code into another representation such as machine code or intermediate representation.

concepts.name: Interpreter
concepts.definition: Executes program instructions through a runtime or interpreter process.

concepts.name: Lexical Analysis
concepts.definition: Turns source text into tokens.

concepts.name: Parsing
concepts.definition: Builds a syntactic representation according to grammar.

concepts.name: AST
concepts.definition: Abstract syntax tree representing program structure.

concepts.name: Type Checking
concepts.definition: Verifies compatibility of types according to language rules.

concepts.name: Optimization
concepts.definition: Transforms code while preserving intended behavior to improve performance, size or other properties.

concepts.name: Linker
concepts.definition: Combines object files and libraries and resolves references into an executable or shared library.

concepts.name: Runtime
concepts.definition: Environment and support system used while a program executes.

concepts.name: Heap
concepts.definition: Tree-based structure commonly used for priority queues.

concepts.name: Binary Search Tree
concepts.definition: Ordered tree supporting search, insert and delete with performance dependent on shape.

concepts.name: Balanced Tree
concepts.definition: Tree whose height is controlled to support efficient operations.

concepts.name: Hashing
concepts.definition: Maps keys to positions using a hash function.

concepts.name: Collision
concepts.definition: Multiple keys map to the same hash location.

concepts.name: Directed Graph
concepts.definition: Graph whose edges have direction.

concepts.name: Undirected Graph
concepts.definition: Graph whose edges do not have direction.

concepts.name: Weighted Graph
concepts.definition: Graph whose edges have associated weights or costs.

concepts.name: BFS
concepts.definition: Breadth-first search explores graph levels outward from a starting node.

concepts.name: DFS
concepts.definition: Depth-first search explores deeply before backtracking.

concepts.name: Dijkstra
concepts.definition: Shortest-path algorithm for graphs with nonnegative edge weights.

concepts.name: Bellman-Ford
concepts.definition: Shortest-path algorithm capable of handling negative edge weights and detecting reachable negative cycles.

concepts.name: Topological Sort
concepts.definition: Ordering of vertices in a directed acyclic graph so every edge goes forward in the order.

concepts.name: Union-Find
concepts.definition: Disjoint-set structure supporting efficient merging and connectivity queries.

concepts.name: Binary Search
concepts.definition: Searches sorted data by repeatedly halving the search region.

concepts.name: Merge Sort
concepts.definition: Divide-and-conquer sorting algorithm with O(n log n) worst-case time and additional memory in common implementations.

concepts.name: Quicksort
concepts.definition: Partition-based sorting algorithm with average O(n log n) behavior under typical assumptions but O(n^2) worst-case without safeguards.
concepts.formula: average O(n log n), worst O(n^2)

concepts.name: Heapsort
concepts.definition: Uses a heap to sort in O(n log n) time and can be implemented in-place.

concepts.name: Dynamic Programming
concepts.definition: Solves overlapping subproblems using memoization or tabulation.

concepts.name: Greedy Algorithm
concepts.definition: Makes locally optimal choices with the expectation that a global optimum results; correctness requires problem-specific proof.

concepts.name: Divide and Conquer
concepts.definition: Split the problem, solve subproblems, then combine results.

concepts.name: Backtracking
concepts.definition: Build candidate solutions incrementally and undo choices when they cannot work.

concepts.name: 1NF
concepts.definition: Atomic values under the chosen relational design.

concepts.name: 2NF
concepts.definition: 1NF plus no partial dependency on part of a composite key.

concepts.name: 3NF
concepts.definition: 2NF plus no inappropriate transitive dependency of non-key attributes.

concepts.name: BCNF
concepts.definition: Every determinant is a candidate key under the formal definition.

concepts.name: Denormalization
concepts.definition: Intentionally introduces redundancy for performance/read simplicity.

concepts.name: Index Tradeoff
concepts.definition: Faster reads can mean additional storage and slower writes/updates.

concepts.name: Transaction Isolation
concepts.definition: Common isolation levels are read uncommitted, read committed, repeatable read and serializable.

concepts.name: Anomalies
concepts.definition: Read anomalies associated with transactions: dirty read, non-repeatable read and phantom read.

concepts.name: Database Migration
concepts.definition: Controlled schema evolution between application versions.

concepts.name: Distributed System
concepts.definition: Multiple networked components cooperate as one logical system.

concepts.name: Latency
concepts.definition: Delay between request and response.

concepts.name: Throughput
concepts.definition: Work completed per unit time.

concepts.name: Availability
concepts.definition: Ability to serve requests when expected.

concepts.name: Consistency
concepts.definition: Whether different clients see compatible versions of data under the chosen consistency model.

concepts.name: Fault Tolerance
concepts.definition: Ability to continue functioning despite component failures.

concepts.name: Replication
concepts.definition: Maintaining copies of data/service state.

concepts.name: Load Balancer
concepts.definition: Distributes work across backend instances.

concepts.name: Scale Out
concepts.definition: Add more machines/instances.

concepts.name: Scale Up
concepts.definition: Increase resources of an existing machine/instance.

concepts.name: Idempotency
concepts.definition: Repeating the same operation has the same intended effect.

concepts.name: Retry
concepts.definition: Repeating failed requests; use carefully to avoid duplicate side effects.

concepts.name: Exponential Backoff
concepts.definition: Increasing delay between retries.

concepts.name: Circuit Breaker
concepts.definition: Stops repeatedly failing calls temporarily to protect a system.

concepts.name: Eventual Consistency
concepts.definition: Replicas may temporarily differ but converge under defined assumptions.

concepts.name: IaaS
concepts.definition: Cloud computing service model known as Infrastructure as a Service.

concepts.name: PaaS
concepts.definition: Cloud computing service model known as Platform as a Service.

concepts.name: SaaS
concepts.definition: Cloud computing service model known as Software as a Service.

concepts.name: Serverless
concepts.definition: Execution model where infrastructure management is largely abstracted from developers; billing/runtime models vary by provider.

concepts.name: Container
concepts.definition: Lightweight isolated process environment sharing the host kernel in common container systems.

concepts.name: Image
concepts.definition: Packaged filesystem/runtime definition used to create containers.

concepts.name: Orchestration
concepts.definition: Managing containers/services at scale.

concepts.name: Kubernetes
concepts.definition: Core Kubernetes concepts include cluster, node, pod, deployment, service, configmap, secret and namespace.

concepts.name: CI
concepts.definition: Frequently integrates changes and runs automated builds/tests.

concepts.name: CD
concepts.definition: Automates delivery or deployment after validation, depending on organizational usage.

concepts.name: Pipeline
concepts.definition: A sequence such as checkout, install dependencies, lint, test, build, package and deploy.

concepts.name: Artifact
concepts.definition: Build output such as APK, AAB, executable, container image, or package.

concepts.name: Rollback
concepts.definition: Return toward a previously working deployment/version.

concepts.name: Blue-Green Deployment
concepts.definition: Two production environments used to reduce deployment risk.

concepts.name: Canary
concepts.definition: Release to a small portion of users/traffic first.

concepts.name: Feature Flag
concepts.definition: Runtime switch enabling/disabling a capability without changing the full build.

concepts.name: Common Commands
concepts.definition: Frequently used Linux commands include pwd, ls, cd, mkdir, touch, cp, mv, rm, cat, less, grep, find, sed, awk, head, tail, chmod, chown, ps, top, kill, curl, wget, ssh and tar.

concepts.name: File Permissions
concepts.definition: Read = r, Write = w, Execute = x, arranged in a typical symbolic layout of owner, group and others.

concepts.name: Process
concepts.definition: A process is a running instance of a program on a Linux system. Use ps, top, or related system tools to inspect processes.

concepts.name: Environment
concepts.definition: PATH tells the shell where to find executable commands.

concepts.name: Shell
concepts.definition: Command interpreter such as Bash, Zsh, PowerShell, etc.

concepts.name: Cherry-Pick
concepts.definition: Applies a selected commit onto another branch.

concepts.name: Stash
concepts.definition: Temporarily stores uncommitted changes.

concepts.name: Reset
concepts.definition: Moves branch references and can modify working/index state depending on mode.

concepts.name: Revert
concepts.definition: Creates a new commit that reverses an earlier commit.

concepts.name: Tag
concepts.definition: Named reference to a specific commit, commonly used for releases.

concepts.name: Semantic Versioning
concepts.definition: Version scheme written as MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, where each part has a defined meaning.

concepts.name: Major
concepts.definition: Version component covering breaking changes.

concepts.name: Minor
concepts.definition: Version component for backward-compatible feature additions.

concepts.name: Patch
concepts.definition: Version component for backward-compatible bug fixes.

concepts.name: API Principles
concepts.definition: API design principles: clear resource model, consistent errors, authentication, authorization, validation, pagination where needed, versioning where appropriate, idempotency where needed, rate limiting and observability; API secrets must never be returned in responses.

concepts.name: Pagination
concepts.definition: Splitting results into pages; common styles are offset-based and cursor-based.

concepts.name: Rate Limiting
concepts.definition: Restricts request frequency.

concepts.name: API Error Response
concepts.definition: Error responses should identify a machine-readable code, a human-readable message, and a request or correlation ID when appropriate.

concepts.name: Session
concepts.definition: Server-side or client-associated authenticated session state.

concepts.name: Token
concepts.definition: Credential used to represent authorization/session state.

concepts.name: Access Token
concepts.definition: Short-lived credential commonly used to access APIs.

concepts.name: Refresh Token
concepts.definition: Credential used to obtain new access credentials where supported.

concepts.name: JWT
concepts.definition: JSON Web Token with encoded claims and signatures; do not confuse encoding with encryption.

concepts.name: OAuth
concepts.definition: Authorization framework for delegated access.

concepts.name: OpenID Connect
concepts.definition: Identity layer built on OAuth 2.0.

concepts.name: Unit Test
concepts.definition: Tests a small unit of behavior in isolation.

concepts.name: Integration Test
concepts.definition: Tests interactions between components.

concepts.name: End-to-End
concepts.definition: Tests a complete user/system workflow.

concepts.name: Regression
concepts.definition: Confirms old functionality remains working after changes.

concepts.name: Property-Based Test
concepts.definition: Tests general properties across many generated inputs.

concepts.name: Fuzz Test
concepts.definition: Feeds varied/unexpected inputs to discover crashes/bugs.

concepts.name: Mock
concepts.definition: Simulated dependency with controlled behavior.

concepts.name: Stub
concepts.definition: Simplified replacement returning predetermined results.

concepts.name: Spy
concepts.definition: Records how it is used.

concepts.name: Test Pyramid
concepts.definition: Generally favor many fast unit tests, fewer integration tests, and fewer expensive end-to-end tests.

concepts.name: Log Levels
concepts.definition: Common log levels are DEBUG, INFO, WARN and ERROR.

concepts.name: Metric
concepts.definition: Numeric measurement over time.

concepts.name: Trace
concepts.definition: Tracks a request across distributed components.

concepts.name: Correlation ID
concepts.definition: Identifier that links related logs/events.

concepts.name: User Flow
concepts.definition: Sequence of steps needed to accomplish a goal.

concepts.name: Affordance
concepts.definition: Visual/interaction cue suggesting how something can be used.

concepts.name: Feedback
concepts.definition: System indication that an action occurred.

concepts.name: Empty State
concepts.definition: UI shown when no data exists.

concepts.name: Loading State
concepts.definition: UI shown while work is in progress.

concepts.name: Error State
concepts.definition: UI shown when work fails.

concepts.name: Success State
concepts.definition: UI shown after successful completion.

concepts.name: Accessibility
concepts.definition: Accessibility principles: readable text, sufficient contrast, clear focus, large enough touch targets, descriptive labels, non-color-only status communication and support for assistive technologies where the platform permits.

concepts.name: Primary Source
concepts.definition: Direct evidence such as original document, measurement, dataset, or official record.

concepts.name: Secondary Source
concepts.definition: Analysis or interpretation of primary material.

concepts.name: Tertiary Source
concepts.definition: Compiled summaries/reference material.

concepts.name: Credibility Questions
concepts.definition: Questions for judging credibility: who produced it, what evidence supports it, when was it produced, is it authoritative for this subject, and can independent evidence verify it?

concepts.name: Correlation Does Not Imply Causation
concepts.definition: Correlation does not necessarily imply causation.

concepts.name: File Extension
concepts.definition: Suffix commonly indicating file type, though extensions alone do not guarantee actual content.

concepts.name: ZIP
concepts.definition: Archive container.

concepts.name: Backup
concepts.definition: A copy intended to support recovery.

concepts.name: Sync
concepts.definition: Keeping data aligned across locations/devices.

concepts.name: Clear Cache
concepts.definition: Removes cached data without necessarily removing all persistent app/user data; behavior depends on platform.

concepts.name: Export
concepts.definition: Create data representation for use elsewhere.

concepts.name: Import
concepts.definition: Bring data into a system.

concepts.name: Personal Data
concepts.definition: Information relating to an identifiable person.

concepts.name: Data Minimization
concepts.definition: Collect only what is needed for the stated purpose.

concepts.name: Retention
concepts.definition: How long information is stored.

concepts.name: Encryption in Transit
concepts.definition: Protects data while moving across a network.

concepts.name: Encryption at Rest
concepts.definition: Protects stored data.

concepts.name: Anonymization
concepts.definition: Transform data so individuals are not reasonably identifiable under a defined risk model.

concepts.name: Pseudonymization
concepts.definition: Replace direct identifiers with pseudonyms; re-identification may still be possible with additional information.

concepts.name: Local Knowledge
concepts.definition: Structured facts/concepts stored on device.

concepts.name: Local Model
concepts.definition: A model executed on-device.

concepts.name: Remote Model
concepts.definition: A model executed on a remote service.

concepts.name: Hybrid AI
concepts.definition: System that selects between local and remote capabilities.

concepts.name: Multimodal
concepts.definition: Model capable of processing multiple data types such as text and images.

concepts.name: Tool Call
concepts.definition: Model/system invokes an external capability.

concepts.name: Agent
concepts.definition: System that can reason over tasks and use tools in a multi-step workflow.
misconceptions: An agent is not automatically more reliable than a non-agent system; tool validation and state management remain necessary.

concepts.name: Private Browsing
concepts.definition: Private browsing mainly reduces local browsing-history traces; it does not make users anonymous to websites, networks, employers, ISPs, or other systems.
misconceptions: Incognito mode makes you anonymous online.
